inputs.text: Organizers say 8 million people attended more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, but there’s no official count, so that figure should be treated as their estimate—not a verdict from the country. Protests are part of civic life; they don’t override elections or the constitutional limits that protect everyone. The language of “defending democracy” may rally opponents of President Donald Trump, but it shouldn’t be used to portray ordinary political disagreement as a threat to vulnerable people. In a republic, lasting change comes through lawful institutions and persuasion, not claims that the loudest crowd speaks for the nation.
